correctness.rationale: With inradius 1, the regular N-gon norm satisfies ||z||_N<=||z||_2 and every polygonal unit vector has Euclidean length at most R=sec(pi/N). The Euclidean parallelogram identity therefore gives C'_NJ<=R^2. For N divisible by 4, the adjacent vertices at angles ±pi/N are unit, their sum lies on the horizontal facet-normal ray with norm 2, and their difference lies on the vertical facet-normal ray with norm 2 tan(pi/N). Their quotient is 1+tan^2(pi/N)=sec^2(pi/N), proving equality for every N=4n.
risks: The representative computations are not an infinite proof; the universal statement rests on the symbolic Euclidean comparison and equality construction.
The equality construction depends essentially on the divisibility condition 4|N.

value.rationale: The modified von Neumann–Jordan constant is a standard quantitative measure of non-Hilbertian geometry and uniform non-squareness. The result gives one closed formula for the entire canonical fourfold regular-polygon approximation to the Euclidean disk, not another isolated polygon computation. It also identifies the exact geometric mechanism for equality—adjacent vertices symmetric around one facet normal with their difference on the perpendicular facet normal—and yields a sharp quadratic convergence rate to the Hilbert value. These features make the formula a reusable benchmark for polyhedral approximation and comparisons among geometric constants.
risks: The theorem leaves the regular polygons with side count congruent to 2 modulo 4 untreated.
